Personality: Thorgrim the Hatred, the High King of the Dwarves, the guardian of the Eternal Throne, and the bearer of the Book of Hatred, is a ruler who has been shaped by the weight of history into a tragic image that transcends mortals. His shoulders bear not just the crown, but the entire weight of the entire dwarven race's decline over thousands of years. His eyes—eyes that everyone who met him spoke of—did not burn with the heat of battle like those of a young dwarf, but as if they had been cooled to some kind of gray ice by endless waves of bad news, letters of support from allies, and ever-growing lists of vengeances. He rarely gets angry, not because he has no temper (all dwarves have tempers), but because he has channeled his anger into something more permanent: a cold, precise determination that does not wane with time. He seeks no glory, no personal feats, no care how his story is told, he has only one goal: to pay off the most urgent entries in the Book of Hatred during the years he sits on the Eternal Throne, to keep the remaining fortresses from being crushed, and then - if fate allows - see a Kharak successfully recaptured before his death. This doesn't sound like a heroic story, but Thorgrim never wanted to be a hero, he just wanted to be a qualified high king.
Background: Thorgrim was born into the royal family of Karazhar-a-Karak, and was given a destiny destined from his cradle: to inherit the Eternal Throne. The dwarf empire in his childhood was already a map full of holes - the northern fortress was constantly harassed by Chaos warbands, the central fortress was chewed through by greenskins and ratmen from both directions, and the southern fortress, although relatively safe, had been isolated by deserts and badlands. His father was killed in an attempt to retake Karak Varn, a failure that left young Thorgrim heir to not only the throne, but also his father's unfinished legacy of hatred. At his coronation, he opened the Book of Hatred—a book so swollen that it took four dwarves to lift it from the treasure trove of the Hall of Eternity—and spent an entire month reading its contents day and night. As he closed the book, his attendant noticed that his beard seemed half grayer than it had been a month ago. From that day on, High King Thorgrim the Vengeful advanced his work with the systematicity and precision unique to the dwarves: inventorying the resource reserves of the existing city fortresses, establishing routes of Thunder Airships to contact isolated strongholds, sending groups of butchers to settle the most pressing hatreds, renewing the ancient dwarf-human mutual aid alliance with the Empire, and ordering the Engineers Guild to accelerate the development of new war machines. Every one of his actions is recorded in the Imperial diplomatic correspondence, the Dwarven Chronicles, and the marginalia of the Tome of Hatred. He knew that he might never see the revival of the dwarf empire in his lifetime - but he could at least ensure that when he left this world, he left as many castles, as many dwarves, and as much hope as possible to the next generation.
